facts.topic: pearl client branch and post-use cooldown
facts.contract: The pearl calls Player::useItem with Throw=4 and the consume flag true before its client/server test. The client skips projectile construction. The later cooldown block requires an actor that is not removed, a nonempty post-use item pointer and cooldown type Use=0. That block calls Player::startItemCooldown(Item,true). An attempted use stopped by the outer cooldown gate never reaches this local item-use block.

facts.topic: pearl consumption uses Instabuild and can empty the last stack before cooldown
facts.contract: Player::useItem consumes one count when its consume flag is true and the effective layered Instabuild ability is false. There is no client/server branch around this decrement. Setting count to zero clears the stack item pointer. Consequently the recovered ordinary count1 pearl path empties the item before the subsequent cooldown test and skips that local cooldown block. A remaining count, or Instabuild preventing consumption, retains the item and can reach the20-tick cooldown. This finding is not a complete inventory-prediction implementation contract.

facts.topic: air-use inventory changes are captured as actions
facts.contract: baseUseItem runs local use inside Container::createTransactionContext. Its container-change callback constructs an InventoryAction with old and new stacks, appends it to the player transaction manager and adds it to the complex transaction. Main-hand actions use ordinary container source0/container0 and the reported slot. The offhand branch uses container119/slot0. The local packet path copies the ItemUse transaction into the payload and applies additional legacy-request metadata. The later air_use_transaction_findings.json closes the selected-item pre-use snapshot and ordinary nonempty selected-slot legacy-tagging chain. Full screen lifecycle and acknowledgement/reconciliation remain unresolved, so an empty-action sender plus a local count decrement is not asserted equivalent.

facts.topic: generic throwable component immediate versus timed use
facts.contract: ThrowableItemComponent installs an OnUse callback. With a positive draw duration it starts the common use timer. Otherwise it invokes _doThrow and reports successful use. _doThrow skips projectile construction on the client, but its client path still reaches swing and consumption logic. Consumption is either Player::useItem(Throw,true) or a direct count decrement protected by Instabuild, depending on the component event flag.

comparison_at_investigation.scope: The parent owns production implementation. These observations identify behavior differences and evidence limits, not an assertion about the eventual source snapshot.
comparison_at_investigation.pearl: Perlin already had incoming cooldown state but ordinary air use did not start this locally predicted built-in cooldown. Existing BedrockSession::Instabuild exposes the relevant ability; using worldBuilder or mayFly would test a different ability.
comparison_at_investigation.inventory: The investigated Perlin air-use sender carried empty action lists and did not predict a count decrement. Native capture of old/new actions is established, but complete authoritative manager and payload framing is not. A local decrement cannot safely be declared complete parity from this evidence alone.
comparison_at_investigation.failed_attempts: The shared native client forwarding path sends the attempted transaction before checking local success. Upstream input eligibility and later server behavior remain separate.
comparison_at_investigation.wind_charge: Specific vanilla component data was not available in this static pass. Generic throwable support does not establish that data.
comparison_at_investigation.mace: No new local smash/Wind Burst impulse is supported by the recovered client branches. Existing server motion handling remains relevant, with its own separate scheduling limits.

limitations: All RVA and branch claims apply to the supplied matching 1.26.51.1/protocol2193 executable and PDB. They are not independent proof for protocol2225 or944.
A local cooldown-only implementation must use the native post-use item-presence condition. For an ordinary consumable pearl this differs between count1, count greater than1, and Instabuild.
The full client inventory manager, legacy request identifiers, item-stack action encoding and acknowledgement reconciliation were not reconstructed in this pass.
No exact mapping from AllowDestructiveObjects enum index40 to a network game-rule key was established.
Held-input reuse is established for pearls through their throwable virtual. This does not establish identical reuse or timing for every instant-use item.
The ItemCompleteUseEvent dynamic listener set and exact first-tick duration ordering remain limited as described in consumable_use_findings.json.
No native executable, server, or anti-cheat acceptance test was run. No entire-item or movement parity guarantee is made.
